# Game Creator Learn — Full Content for AI Ingestion

> Game Creator Learn is a free, browser-based AI tool that generates complete playable educational HTML5 games. Users configure learning parameters through a sidebar interface, and the app assembles a detailed prompt sent to a user-chosen LLM provider to produce a single-file HTML game. No signup, no backend, no server-side API keys required — all generation happens client-side in the browser. Users bring their own API keys (BYOK model).

URL: https://aigamecreatorlearn.netlify.app/
GitHub: https://github.com/alvescrafter/game-creator-learn
Pricing: Free (users supply their own LLM API keys; local providers like Ollama and LM Studio are completely free)
Language: English (British English spelling)
Currency: GBP (£)

---

## How It Works

Game Creator Learn is an Educational Game Prompt Orchestrator. It does NOT generate games itself — it assembles a detailed, structured prompt from user configuration and sends it to the user's chosen AI provider (OpenAI, Gemini, Claude, Ollama, LM Studio, or a custom OpenAI-compatible API). The LLM then generates a complete, standalone HTML5 game.

### Generation Process
1. User configures educational parameters in the sidebar (6 modules)
2. App assembles a detailed system prompt + user prompt from the configuration
3. Prompt is sent to the user's configured LLM provider via client-side fetch()
4. LLM generates a complete HTML5 game (single file, all CSS/JS embedded)
5. Game is rendered live in an iframe sandbox
6. User can refine the game via multi-turn conversation with the LLM
7. User can download the game as a standalone HTML file

### Refinement Process
- After generating, users type a change request (e.g., "Add a quiz at the end of each level")
- The app sends the previous game code + the refinement request to the LLM
- The LLM regenerates the game with the changes applied
- This can be repeated iteratively

---

## Sidebar Modules (6)

### Module 1: Educational Topic
The most important module — drives the entire game's learning content.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Subject | 12 subjects: Maths, English, Physics, Biology, Chemistry, History, Geography, Computer Science, Art, Music, Foreign Languages, Other |
| Specific Topic | Free text — describe the specific topic (e.g., "Fractions", "Photosynthesis", "Shakespeare's Sonnets") |
| Learning Objective | Free text — what the student should learn (e.g., "Understand how to add fractions with different denominators") |

### Module 2: Difficulty & Age Range
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Age Range | 5–8 years (KS1/Early), 9–11 years (KS2/Primary), 12–15 years (KS3/Lower Secondary), 16–18 years (KS4-5/GCSE–A Level), University, Masters/Postgraduate |
| Difficulty Level | Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced, Expert |
| Accessibility Notes | Free text — specify accessibility needs (e.g., "Dyslexia-friendly fonts", "Colour-blind safe", "Large text for young readers") |

The age range affects vocabulary complexity, content depth, and UI design. The AI automatically adjusts language and difficulty to match the selected age group.

### Module 3: Core Identity
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Game Type | Reliable educational types: Quiz/Trivia, Practice Challenge, Puzzle, Matching Game, Memory Game, Sorting Game, Typing Game, Word Search, Escape Room, Adventure Quiz, Board Game, Platformer Quiz, Racing Quiz, Card Game |
| Setting / Theme | Free text — describe your game world (e.g., "Space Explorer Maths", "Chemistry Lab Adventure") |
| Tone | Slider from Serious/Academic (0) to Playful/Fun (100) |

### Module 4: Mechanics & Gameplay
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Mechanics | Click-to-toggle tags: Multiple Choice, Type Answer, Fill-in-the-Blank, Matching, Sorting & Categorisation, Sequencing, Drag & Drop, Timed Challenge, Hint System, Level Progression, Lives / Attempts, Collectibles, Dialogue Prompts, Spaced Review, Achievements |
| Specific Rules | Free text — custom rules (e.g., "Player earns stars for correct answers, loses a life for wrong ones") |
| Difficulty Curve | Gentle Ramp, Steady Progression, Adaptive Review, Challenge Rounds |

### Module 5: Visual & Aesthetic
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Art Style | Pixel Art, Minimalist Vector, ASCII, Simple 2D Shapes, Hand-drawn, Flat Design, Retro CRT, Neon Glow, Cartoon, Whiteboard/Chalkboard |
| Color Palette | Pick Primary, Secondary, and Background colors |
| Visual Effects | Free text — describe VFX (e.g., "Confetti on correct answer", "Star particles on level up") |

### Module 6: Audio & Soundscape
| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Music Mood | Lo-fi, Orchestral, 8-bit/Chiptune, Cheerful, Ambient, No Music |
| SFX Requirements | Free text — describe sound effects (e.g., "Ding for correct answer", "Buzz for wrong answer") |

Each module has a toggle switch — turn off any module you don't want included in the prompt.

---

## LLM Providers (6)

All providers are configured client-side. Users bring their own API keys (BYOK). Keys are stored in localStorage and never sent to any server.

### 1. OpenAI
- Models: gpt-4o, gpt-4o-mini, gpt-4-turbo, gpt-4, gpt-3.5-turbo, o1, o1-mini, o3-mini
- Default model: gpt-4o
- API key required: Yes
- Supports model listing: Yes (fetches /models endpoint)
- API format: OpenAI native

### 2. Google Gemini
- Models: gemini-2.5-pro-preview-03-25, gemini-2.0-flash, gemini-2.0-flash-lite, gemini-1.5-pro, gemini-1.5-flash
- Default model: gemini-2.0-flash
- API key required: Yes
- Supports model listing: Yes
- API format: OpenAI-compatible endpoint

### 3. Anthropic Claude
- Models: claude-sonnet-4-20250514, claude-3-7-sonnet-20250219, claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022, claude-3-5-haiku-20241022, claude-3-opus-20240229
- Default model: claude-sonnet-4-20250514
- API key required: Yes
- Supports model listing: No
- API format: Anthropic native (converted from OpenAI format internally)

### 4. Ollama (Local)
- Models: llama3.2, llama3.1, llama3, mistral, codellama, gemma2, phi3, qwen2, deepseek-coder-v2, mixtral
- Default model: llama3.2
- API key required: No (runs locally)
- Supports model listing: Yes
- API format: OpenAI-compatible
- Default endpoint: http://localhost:11434

### 5. LM Studio (Local)
- Models: Populated dynamically from server
- Default model: (auto-detected)
- API key required: No (runs locally)
- Supports model listing: Yes
- API format: OpenAI-compatible
- Default endpoint: http://localhost:1234

### 6. Custom API
- Models: User-specified
- Default model: User-specified
- API key required: Depends on endpoint
- Supports model listing: Yes
- API format: OpenAI-compatible
- Endpoint: User-specified

## Keyboard Shortcuts

| Shortcut | Action |
|----------|--------|
| Ctrl + Enter | Generate Educational Game |
| Ctrl + B | Toggle Sidebar |
| Ctrl + H | Open History |
| Ctrl + T | Open Templates |
| Ctrl + , | Open API Settings |
| Escape | Close modals / Exit fullscreen |

## Educational Game Best Practices

### Choosing the Right Game Type
- Quiz/Trivia — Best for knowledge recall and fact-based learning (vocabulary, dates, definitions)
- Puzzle — Great for problem-solving and logical thinking (maths, coding concepts)
- Platformer Quiz / Racing Quiz — Adds simple action while keeping questions as the learning gate
- Practice Challenge — Best for repeated skill practice with fast feedback and mastery goals
- Escape Room — Excellent for collaborative problem-solving and critical thinking
- Card Game — Good for matching, categorisation, and memory-based learning

### Setting Age-Appropriate Content
- 5–8 years: Simple vocabulary, large text, bright colours, short activities, lots of positive reinforcement
- 9–11 years: More complex concepts, longer activities, introduction of scoring systems
- 12–15 years: Abstract thinking, multi-step problems, competitive elements
- 16–18 years: Exam-revision style, detailed feedback, progress tracking
- University: Complex scenarios, research-based challenges, in-depth analysis
- Masters/Postgraduate: Advanced simulations, case studies, professional-level content

### Writing Effective Learning Objectives
Good learning objectives are specific and measurable:
- Good: "Understand how to add fractions with different denominators"
- Good: "Identify the main organs of the human digestive system"
- Good: "Apply Newton's second law to calculate force"
- Poor: "Learn about maths" (too vague)
- Poor: "Know science" (not measurable)

---

## Example Configurations

### Maths Quiz for 9-11 Year Olds
- Subject: Maths
- Topic: Multiplication Tables
- Learning Objective: "Recall multiplication facts up to 12×12 quickly and accurately"
- Age Range: 9–11 years (KS2/Primary)
- Difficulty: Beginner
- Game Type: Quiz
- Mechanics: Multiple Choice, Timed Challenge, Hint System, Level Progression

### Biology Escape Room for 16-18 Year Olds
- Subject: Biology
- Topic: Cell Biology
- Learning Objective: "Identify organelles and explain their functions in eukaryotic cells"
- Age Range: 16–18 years (KS4-5/GCSE–A Level)
- Difficulty: Advanced
- Game Type: Escape Room
- Mechanics: Hint System, Dialogue Prompts, Sequencing, Spaced Review

### Physics Platformer Quiz for 12-15 Year Olds
- Subject: Physics
- Topic: Forces and Motion
- Learning Objective: "Apply the relationship between force, mass, and acceleration"
- Age Range: 12–15 years (KS3/Lower Secondary)
- Difficulty: Intermediate
- Game Type: Platformer Quiz
- Mechanics: Multiple Choice, Collectibles, Level Progression, Hint System

---

## Generated Game Structure

All generated games follow a mandatory structure:

1. Start Menu Screen — title, Start button, How to Play button, Settings button
2. Game Screen — HUD with score/lives/level/timer, Pause button, ESC key support
3. Pause Menu — Resume, Restart, How to Play, Main Menu, ESC to resume
4. Game Over / Level Complete Screen — score, learning summary, Play Again, Main Menu
5. Standardised Buttons — primary/secondary/danger styles, 44px minimum, emoji icons
6. Keyboard Controls — ESC, Enter, Arrow/WASD, Space
7. Responsive Design — desktop + mobile
8. Single HTML File — no external dependencies, all assets via code, no CDN links

---

## Technical Details

- All games are generated as single HTML files containing all CSS and JavaScript
- Games use Vanilla JS/Canvas for rendering and game logic
- No external dependencies or build tools required
- Games run directly in the browser — just open the downloaded HTML file
- Generation and refinement use the user's configured AI provider
- Token limit: 50,000 tokens per generation
- Streaming support: real-time streaming responses from LLM providers
- History: last 50 generated games saved to localStorage
- Templates: save and reuse game configurations (localStorage)
- Connection testing: verify API keys and detect available models before use

---

## Tech Stack

- Frontend: Vanilla HTML, CSS, JavaScript — no frameworks, no build tools
- Storage: localStorage (state, API settings, history, templates)
- Rendering: Vanilla DOM manipulation + Canvas (via generated games)
- LLM APIs: 6 provider adapters (OpenAI-compatible + Anthropic native format)
- Generation: Prompt assembly → LLM call → Code extraction → iframe rendering
- Deployment: Static site on Netlify
- Testing: Jest (prompt builder tests)
- Launcher: Pinokio support via pinokio.json

---

## Pricing

- Free — no cost, no signup, no account required
- Users supply their own LLM API keys (BYOK model)
- Local providers (Ollama, LM Studio) are completely free to use
- No hidden costs, no premium tier, no token system
